entities.summary:
A phenomenon in which the soul (astral body) is said to exit the physical body, the out-of-body experience has been a subject of fascination and spiritual seeking across cultures and continents since the dawn of human history.

The concept of out-of-body experiences dates back to ancient civilizations, where it was often associated with mysticism, mysticism, and the quest for divine knowledge. In many ancient cultures, including ancient Egypt, Greece, and China, out-of-body experiences were seen as a means to access higher states of consciousness and communicate with the divine.

In the Western tradition, the out-of-body experience has been a central theme in the work of philosophers such as Plato and Plotinus, who saw it as a means to access the realm of forms and gain insight into the nature of reality.

In modern times, the out-of-body experience has been studied extensively in the fields of parapsychology and psychology, with many researchers attempting to explain its causes and mechanisms. Despite its long history, the out-of-body experience remains a subject of debate and controversy, with some seeing it as a legitimate aspect of human consciousness and others dismissing it as a mere fantasy or hallucination.

The out-of-body experience has left a lasting legacy in the realm of spirituality and consciousness, influencing the development of various mystical and esoteric traditions, including Theosophy and the New Age movement. Its impact can be seen in the work of influential thinkers such as Emanuel Swedenborg and Rudolf Steiner, who built upon the idea of out-of-body experiences in their own philosophical and spiritual systems.
